specGaps: SG-A — THE §3.8 BANNER DOES NOT EXIST AND NO TASK EVER LANDS IT. plan:2966 orders the smoke to 'Observe and record … the conductor banner (§3.8)', but at HEAD nothing emits one (see verifiedAgainstHead row 1: no doctrine instruction, and renderStateBlock carries none of version/runId/model; GateRun has no id and InjectCtx has no model). Every plan mention of the banner (421, 1487-1491, 1818, 3089, 3367) is descriptive; no task bullet assigns it. Same class of hole as C-041 on Branch B. RESOLUTION: 13.2 lands it, TEST-FIRST, under the plan's own Step-2 mechanism, as the FIRST 13.2 task-let (before the smoke is re-captured), with this exact shape so no implementer has to guess — (i) `InjectCtx` gains three required fields `{version: string, runId: string | null, model: string}`; (ii) `renderStateBlock` prepends ONE line, first line of the block, of the exact form `conductor v<version> · run <runId> · model <model>` (runId rendered as `none` when null, i.e. before a run exists), everything else in the block unchanged; (iii) conductor/doctrine/core.md gains one short instruction: the FIRST response in any session opens with that banner line copied VERBATIM from the live state block and nothing else on that line; (iv) tests: a new case in conductor/tests/inject.test.ts asserting the state block's first line for both the runId-present and runId-null cases and that buildSystemAppend still ends with the block, plus a doctrine.test.ts anchor for the core.md instruction. Rationale for the location: the state block is the only channel that is re-stated every request (G9) and already the only place the session learns run facts, and core.md is already the orchestrator's bound prompt in the opencode fragment. Rationale for doing it here rather than 'fixing 8.2': editing a file first added by an earlier task's commit is an M6 hard stop needing written justification — this gap IS that justification, and it is recorded in CORRECTIONS.md when the task-let lands. NOTE the honest limit that survives: the banner is a MODEL-PRODUCED line, so its absence in one response proves the model skipped an instruction, not that the plugin is dead; the BEACON (row 13.2-liveness-beacon) is the mechanical half and the artifact must lean on it.

SG-B — HOW IS OPENCODE DRIVEN, AND WHERE DOES A VERBATIM TRANSCRIPT COME FROM? plan:2965 says only 'run opencode with a toy prompt', while M8 demands verbatim command lines and raw output. opencode 1.18.15 offers both an interactive TUI (`opencode [project]`) and a headless `opencode run [message..]`; the TUI leaves no stdout transcript, and headless `run` cannot answer an interactive ask. RESOLUTION: the smoke is driven in the TUI, because 12.2's first-run setup asks TWO questions that have NO default (git mode, behavioralPaths confirmation, plan:2906-2908) and §3.6's edit-permission asks are part of the path under test — a headless run would either deadlock or need `--auto`, which disables the very gate being smoked. The RECORD is therefore assembled from four verbatim sources, all of which are copy-pasteable commands: (1) the shell commands that launched everything (serve.py, cd, opencode) with their cwd; (2) opencode's own log, captured by launching with `--print-logs --log-level INFO` and teeing stderr to a file whose path is named; (3) `opencode export <sessionID>` for the conversation itself (the sessionID is read from `.conductor/state/alive.json` and from `opencode session`), pasted or attached with its raw output — and if export fails, the failure is pasted verbatim and the artifact says the conversation is unavailable rather than reconstructing it; (4) the on-disk artifacts (`.conductor/runs/<runId>/{run.json,journal.jsonl,items/*.json,questions.jsonl,report.md}` and the scratch repo's `git log`), which are the AUTHORITATIVE record for every claim about state — the chat is context, the ledger is evidence. The typed prompts are recorded exactly as typed, including their typos.

SG-C — ARTIFACT PATH. plan:2966 says `conductor/SMOKE.md` while this build's only other live artifact sits at conductor/docs/RUNNER-DISCOVERY.md and §1.1's tree puts docs under conductor/docs/. RESOLUTION: honour the plan literally — `conductor/SMOKE.md` — because §11's acceptance row (plan:3136) also says 'SMOKE.md' and a relocated artifact is exactly the kind of drift verify-acceptance.sh's 'every live artifact present' check trips over. Recorded so the Phase 13 gate does not treat the top-level placement as a mistake.

SG-D — THE SCRATCH REPO IS UNSPECIFIED. plan:2965 says only 'cd to a scratch repo'. RESOLUTION, pinned so the run is reproducible and cannot damage this repository: a FRESH git repo created OUTSIDE llama-harness (under the session scratchpad, never inside .data/ or .out/ and never inside this worktree), with exactly (a) `package.json` naming `node --test` so 12.2's detection has something real to find, (b) one committed source file and one committed passing test so the runner is provably green BEFORE the smoke, (c) a `README.md` containing ONE deliberately introduced typo, committed, so prompt 2 has a real subject, and (d) an initial commit — `git -C <scratch> log --oneline` pasted before and after. The artifact pastes the full creation transcript. llama-harness itself is NEVER the workspace: `git -C <llama-harness> status --porcelain` is pasted before and after the smoke and must differ only by the files 13.2 declares.

SG-E — PROMPT 2 MIGHT NOT TAKE THE NON-BEHAVIORAL PATH. 'fix the typo in the README' can legitimately classify as `trivial` (a full trivialItem riding EXECUTING(trivial) to report-lite) rather than as a work run carrying a `behavioral:false` item — the two are different §2.4/§2.5 paths and only the SECOND is what §11's acceptance row (plan:3137, 'the non-behavioral path exercised') names. RESOLUTION: record what the model actually did, verbatim, and never edit the classification by hand or re-roll silently. If attempt 1 classified trivial, the artifact records that outcome IN FULL (it is a real datum about the classifier), then a second attempt is made with a prompt whose scope is unambiguously a work run over docs only (e.g. a README typo plus a docs/ correction), and BOTH attempts appear in SMOKE.md. The §11 row is marked MET only if some recorded attempt actually walked an item with `behavioral:false` from PENDING through PUBLISHED with no test ever written; otherwise the row is marked UNMET with the reason. An unmet acceptance row honestly recorded is a pass for this task; a row claimed on a run that did not happen is the worst outcome available.

SG-F — WHAT DOES STEP 2 COMMIT? plan:2974-2975 orders each fix to land 'as its own red->green task-let with a test at the layer that failed', then names ONE commit, `conductor: 13.2 live smoke`. Those cannot both be single commits. RESOLUTION, following the 12.1-G5 precedent already in STATE.json: each fix becomes its OWN non-manifest STATE.json row `13.2-fix-<n>` (manifest:false) with its own red test, its own full-gate green (`bash scripts/test-conductor.sh`, both node and bun legs — G14), its own diff read, and its own commit `conductor: 13.2 fix <n> — <layer>`; the MANIFEST commit `conductor: 13.2 live smoke` lands conductor/SMOKE.md (plus docs/build state) and nothing else. C-007 already establishes that extra commits do not disturb verify-acceptance.sh's 'each of the 52 manifest messages appears exactly once' check. Any fix that touches a file first added by an earlier task's commit is an M6 hard stop and gets a CORRECTIONS.md entry naming the file and the reason.

SG-G — WHAT IF THE SMOKE CANNOT COMPLETE? A 27B local model may fail schema validation past MAX_ATTEMPTS, wedge on a gate, or exhaust the futile-re-prompt counter. RESOLUTION (inherited from the 11.8 ruling and from branch-b-plan.md's attempt-once rule): a BLOCKED smoke is an acceptable, committable result. The artifact records the exact stopping point, the last legal tool, the stop kind, the stop-report if one was written, and every command attempted with its raw output; §11's acceptance rows are then individually marked MET / UNMET with evidence. ALL attempts are recorded, in order, including abandoned ones — publishing only the best-looking attempt is fabrication by selection. Retrying the whole smoke after a Step-2 fix is expected and each re-run is dated and labelled.

SG-H — 'NOTE RETRY COUNTS' (plan:2967) IS UNDERSPECIFIED. RESOLUTION: retry counts are MACHINE-DERIVED, never eyeballed. The artifact pastes a command over `.conductor/runs/<runId>/journal.jsonl` (a grep/jq one-liner is fine; its exact text and raw output must both appear) producing, per sub-session: role, schema name, attempts, and terminal outcome, plus the totals — total sub-sessions dispatched, total `subsession.retry` lines, count that reached `attempts: 3`, count that ended in `subsession.abort`. At least one full `subsession.retry` line is pasted verbatim INCLUDING its `errors` payload, because the shape of the validation error is the POC datum a reader actually needs.

SG-I — WHICH SOURCE PROVES G13 (one model, many roles)? The clean source is the router's metrics ledger (Task 11.7), whose per-request `model`/`role` fields cover every sub-session — but only if the smoke runs WITH the router. RESOLUTION: run the smoke with the router in the loop (serve.py's default when the binary exists, per plan:2878), and use the ledger as the primary source; if the router is unavailable for any reason, the artifact says so and falls back to the exported session's per-message model field, explicitly naming which source each number came from. A number whose source is not named does not belong in the artifact.

SG-J — IDLE CONTINUATION MAY NOT FIRE ON ITS OWN. plan:2967 requires 'idle continuation firing at least once', but a session that keeps working never goes idle. RESOLUTION: do NOT synthesize it — no hand-typed 'continue', no fabricated journal line. The operator lets a session sit idle at a point where `legalTools(...).recommended` is non-null (the design's own trigger, Task 10.1) and waits out the debounce, recording the wall-clock wait. Admissible evidence is a `continuation`/`reprompt` journal line whose payload names the recommended tool, plus the tool call that followed it with no human input in between. If it still never fires, that is a genuine finding about 10.1, recorded as UNMET with the wait time, and fixed under Step 2.

SG-K — SINGLE WRITER (G6) DURING A LIVE SMOKE. `.conductor/state/run.lock` admits one writer; a second opencode session opened in the same scratch repo (easy to do by accident while inspecting things) would take the read-only path and could make the artifact describe two different runs. RESOLUTION: exactly ONE opencode session at a time per scratch repo for the duration of each recorded run; inspection is done with plain shell commands (cat/git/jq) in a separate terminal, never a second opencode. If a second session was opened at any point, the artifact says so and names the runId each observation belongs to.
